R_H1.passageTitle: What a Fund Reveals in Its Documents

passages.label: A
passages.text: A mutual fund pools money from many people who invest under a common plan. Professional advisers decide which assets the fund will hold, and some funds own stocks and shares, while others hold bonds or other assets. A share gives a buyer a part of the pool, and an investment can rise or fall in value, so it is useful to understand the fund’s aim and the financial risk before a purchase is made.

passages.label: B
passages.text: A prospectus explains how a fund aims to make money and when a customer might lose money. Someone may save money for a future payment or invest money with a longer goal in mind. If a buyer has a loan or other debt, the time for repayment can affect that decision. Reading about each service can help a person ask whether they would need to borrow money for spending in the near future.

passages.label: C
passages.text: Some funds seek income from bonds. Other funds aim for assets to rise in value. Some want both. These aims influence what a manager buys. The prospectus also explains the risks that come with those choices. A fund that puts money into a single industry may face a different risk from one that puts money into many industries. The investor can look for a link between the aim, the way the manager works and what might cause a loss. A name by itself cannot show that link. Some funds aim for a small gain over many years. Others may see prices go up and down much faster. A reader can look for the part of the document that explains those changes.

passages.label: D
passages.text: A table in the prospectus lists fees and expenses. The SEC asks funds to use this table. Some fees are paid when people buy shares. Annual operating expenses come out of the fund's assets, so people may pay them indirectly. Funds can charge different amounts for the same kind of service. Costs lower the return to the people who hold shares. A high-cost fund has to do better to leave its buyers with the same result as a low-cost one. The table offers a common format for making that comparison.

passages.label: E
passages.text: Past figures show how a fund did at a time when prices and the market were different. An interest rate may change. The price of the things the fund owns can rise or fall. A buyer who can afford to invest part of their savings may need other money for expenditure in the near future. The time until that money is needed is one factor to consider. It helps to read the results with the aims and the list of charges. A good year previously does not show what a fund will be worth next year.

R_H2.passageTitle: A Record Sale of a Rare Car

passages.label: A
passages.text: On 5 May 2022, a Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé was sold at an auction in Stuttgart for 135 million euros. RM Sotheby's worked with Mercedes-Benz on the sale, held at the company's museum, and the buyer was a private collector. The auction house announced the result later that month as a record car sale, and the extremely valuable vehicle was one of only two prototypes built in 1955. Its name included that of Rudolf Uhlenhaut, the engineer associated with its creation, and this was a particular historical object, rather than an ordinary car available in large numbers. The announcements clearly identified the model and its year of construction.

passages.label: B
passages.text: The company had owned the car since it was built. Among the people invited to the sale were selected customers and international collectors of cars and art. The purchase therefore occurred in a specialist collecting market, with a very limited supply of this model, and a buyer able to pay that amount was clearly wealthy, but the sale did not describe what most drivers could afford. Nor did it provide a price for every old Mercedes. People at the sale knew the history of this exact car. Someone who chose to invest in an everyday car would face a very different market.

passages.label: C
passages.text: The sale was a decision to raise money, and the other car stayed in the company’s museum, and a buyer may be a millionaire yet still need to choose how to make a payment. Collectors who spend money on a car also pay for a service such as safe storage. Someone who tries to invest money in a rare car may make money or lose money at a later sale. That possibility will affect whether they are prepared to take out a loan.

passages.label: D
passages.text: The company said it would use the money from the sale to start the Mercedes-Benz Fund, and the fund would help young people learn and carry out research related to the environment, including work on cutting carbon emissions. Money and help from someone with more experience could go to school pupils and people studying at university. The company also said it wanted to help people who could not pay for such work on their own. These were plans for how the money would be used. The company announced where the revenue would go.

passages.label: E
passages.text: The record shows what someone paid for one car on one day. The history of the car was one factor, and the small supply was another. Anyone who buys one as an investment may pay to store and insure it. Those costs are part of the buyer’s expenditure. A buyer would need that financial record and a later sale price to work out the return. A professional might offer an estimate of the car’s value today. An estimate cannot tell us what a sale will raise in the future.

R_H3.passageTitle: Reading the Figures behind Household Income

passages.label: A
passages.text: In September 2025, the United States Census Bureau gave its estimate for real median household income in 2024. It was 83,730 dollars. Median refers to the point in the middle when households are put in order of income. It is different from adding up all the incomes and dividing by the number of households. Real means that the figure takes price changes into account. The amount printed for 2024 differed from the 2023 estimate. The Bureau found that the gap was not large enough to show a statistically significant change. The figures came from a survey of some households. The Bureau uses their answers to describe a much larger group of households across the country.

passages.label: B
passages.text: The report looked at income for a whole household rather than the pay of one person. Its main income measure used money before taxes, and it did not count money that people already held in savings. The report also gave figures for people who worked full time throughout the year. Those figures leave out many people who did some work but did not work in that way for the whole year. A reader needs to know who is included before comparing the two measures.

passages.label: C
passages.text: The report also examined inequality, meaning differences across the income distribution. Income at the point above ninety per cent of households increased, while the middle and the lower point reported did not change significantly. At the same time, the overall inequality measure used in the report did not change significantly. These findings could exist together because they described different aspects of the distribution. One statistic did not contain every detail about how groups had changed. The value of a national income figure therefore depended partly on understanding what it summarised.

passages.label: D
passages.text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported 2024 household expenditure on housing, food, transport and healthcare. Housing took the largest share. A person earning the minimum wage might find it hard to save money after a regular rent payment. A household could decide to borrow money or take out a loan, creating debt someone is responsible for paying. The decision to spend money on these essentials can look very different across families. The spending survey adds context, although it uses a different unit from the Census income table. Researchers can also ask whether typical households can put aside money after spending on essential goods, since regional costs can affect that comparison in substantial ways.

passages.label: E
passages.text: The Census Bureau also gave an official poverty rate based on money income. The financial threshold depends on how many people are in a family and who they are. Employment and hours worked affect how much money comes in. Prices affect what that money can buy. Even a family near the middle may struggle to afford a home where demand is high. This is one reason the same amount of money can support a different standard of living in different places. A table may tell us about one factor in the economy while leaving another out.
